series: New listing #19 (Oct 6), CMO slate Oct 8 pm; H01 your price pays less than you think
hook: $14,850 of rent came in. The house kept $550
hook_say: Here is what one rental house really kept from a year of rent.

rows.label: Rent received, Oak Street House
rows.why: The spreadsheet's sample year for one house, Oak Street: $14,850 of rent logged on the 2 Log tab.

rows.label: Expenses, Schedule E lines
rows.why: Mortgage interest, property taxes, insurance, repairs and the other Schedule E lines add up to $10,006.

rows.label: Profit before depreciation
rows.why: Rent minus those expenses: $4,844 of profit before depreciation.

rows.label: Mortgage principal
rows.why: Mortgage principal is not an expense, but the cash still leaves: $2,844.

rows.label: Capital improvement
rows.why: A $1,450 capital improvement is cash out too, even though it is not a repair expense.

rows.label: Cash flow, what you kept
rows.why: After principal and the improvement, the house kept $550 for the year. The P&L tab shows both numbers side by side for every property.

cta.title: Rental Property Spreadsheet
cta.say: Search ProofNotFluff for the full workbook.

note: Sample property in the file. Estimates for organizing, not tax advice.

sources.source: 4 Property P&L G25 (Rent) and G27 (Total money in), Oak Street House
4 Property P&L G43, total expenses (Schedule E lines)
4 Property P&L G44, profit before depreciation
4 Property P&L G48, cash flow (what you kept); O59 550
